sentences.text: Heterodontosaurus was a small dinosaur that grew between 1.18 and 1.75 meters long and weighed between 2 and 10 kilograms.
The most complete skeleton of this species measured approximately 1.18 meters in length.
This animal possessed a small but robust skull.
Unlike its relatives, this dinosaur experienced sporadic rather than continuous tooth replacement.
It possessed long arms with large, curved claws that could help it seize small prey.
The species Heterodontosaurus tucki was named in 1962 based on a skull found in South Africa.
The holotype specimen, which serves as the primary reference for the species, was discovered during a British-South African expedition in 1961–1962.
Heterodontosaurus was first described in 1962 as a primitive member of the order Ornithischia.
The genus Heterodontosaurus was named by Charning and Crompton in 1962.
Heterodontosaurus is commonly considered a herbivorous dinosaur.
The unique teeth and jaws of heterodontosaurines were specialized for processing plant material with a sophistication comparable to later ornithischians.
Researchers suggest Heterodontosaurus specialized in tough plant material due to its dentition, while the related Abrictosaurus likely ate softer vegetation.
Heterodontosaurus is now considered to have been bipedal, although it was previously thought to be capable of quadrupedal movement.
In 1980, Santa Luca described features of the forelimb implying strong arm musculature in Heterodontosaurus.
Santa Luca proposed that Heterodontosaurus moved quadrupedally when slow but could switch to a faster bipedal run.
Researchers suggest the robust arms of Heterodontosaurus were adapted for foraging, possibly by digging up roots and breaking insect nests.
Heterodontosaurus had a neck made of nine vertebrae that formed an S-shaped curve.
Heterodontosaurus is the namesake and best-known member of the family Heterodontosauridae.
Sereno defined Heterodontosauridae as a clade in 1998 and 2005 based on skull features like few premaxillary teeth, caniniform teeth, and a jugal horn.
Heterodontosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic period, approximately 200 to 190 million years ago.
Heterodontosaurids existed from the Late Triassic to the Early Cretaceous, spanning at least 100 million years.
In 1970, Richard A. Thulborn suggested that Heterodontosaurus was a junior synonym of the genus Lycorhinus.
Researchers suggest Heterodontosaurus may have had lip-like structures rather than bridging skin between the jaws.
In 1974, Thulborn suggested the tusks were likely used for combat, display, or defense rather than feeding.
In 2017, Matthew G. Baron and colleagues suggested grouping ornithischians with theropods in Ornithoscelida based on similarities between Heterodontosaurus and Eoraptor.
In 1974 and 1978, Thulborn found no evidence of continuous tooth replacement in known skulls, suggesting teeth formed simultaneously.
Thulborn hypothesized that complete tooth replacement occurred only during aestivation, a period when the animal did not feed.
